classification: protocol interpretation, resolved from the registered text, the registered implementation and the registered §12.2 records. Not an amendment: nothing registered changes, and no threshold, caliper, band or criterion moves.

implementation_basis.gates.admit_family: `pre = prescreen.get(q)` then `if pre is None: reasons.append("no pre-screen measurement")` --- reject, not abstain
implementation_basis.regime.assert_shortlist_is_measured: added with this artifact; refuses to write a REGIME_SCREEN record whose shortlist names a rung the ladder curves do not carry, which puts the guarantee on the mandatory path rather than in a docstring
implementation_basis.regime.shortlist: skips a rung with no measured value, so the shortlist is a subset of the measured rungs by construction

prior_statements_corrected: dci1/reports/cal_screen_v4/REPORT.md §6 called this a preregistration gap of the same kind as §12.4's graded clause and reported abstain and reject as co-equal readings. It is not a gap. The screen met unmeasured rungs because it admitted rungs outside the §12.2 shortlist and because its floored-stem pre-screen came from a screen that measured only some rungs --- both properties of the screen, not of the protocol.
dci1/reports/INVESTIGATION_2026-08-20.md named this reading the smallest remaining blocker. It is not a blocker.
question: §13.2 condition 2 checks the reference-minus-A distance on the disjoint 24 pre-screen topics. Two non-confirmatory screens reported that some rungs had no such measurement and that the protocol does not say whether an unmeasurable condition abstains or fails.

registered_disposition_executed.probe: one rung of RF1 with every other condition satisfied; the only difference between the two runs is whether that rung has a pre-screen value
registered_disposition_executed.registered_disposition: reject: a rung with no pre-screen measurement collects a rejection reason and is not admitted

resolution: The case does not arise in the registered pipeline. §12.2 measures all 94 reference rungs on the 24 pre-screen topics and writes the shortlist; §12.3 measures only shortlisted severities on the 96 calibration topics; §13.2 condition 1 is a caliper on that 96-topic measurement, so §13.2's feasible set is a subset of §12.2's shortlist and every member of it carries a pre-screen value. Condition 2 is always evaluable. Where the case is nevertheless constructed, the registered implementation rejects.

textual_basis.\u00a712.2: the pre-screen measures on the 24 pre-screen topics, one draw per cell: the full n grid for A, the full m grid for B, and all 94 reference ladder severities ... and produces the shortlist of at most three ladder severities per family
textual_basis.\u00a712.3: on the 96 solo-calibration topics at M_cal = 4 ... the full n grid, the full m grid, and every shortlisted reference severity are measured
textual_basis.\u00a713.2 condition 1: that absolute difference is at most 0.10 on the 96 solo-calibration topics
textual_basis.\u00a713.2 condition 2: the same absolute difference is at most 0.15 on the disjoint 24 pre-screen topics

what_this_does_not_decide: which family or severity is admitted on any model

what happens under a prompt stem other than the registered one: a stem change is a change of experimental condition, so §12.1, §12.2, §12.3 and §13.2 are all re-measured under it (Amendment A §5.1 says so itself). §12.2 re-run under the new stem supplies condition 2's input exactly as it does now, so the resolution holds under any stem and is not an argument for or against one.
